text:
maria: Heads-up — after enabling the FP8 kernel on L40s for orion-7b we see a consistent drop on our summarization eval set. small repro and numbers below. anyone seen a similar pattern?

aj: which eval and what delta?

maria: matthews-sum eval (1k queries). baseline (INT8-GPTQ) rouge-1=41.2, fp8-kernel rollout rouge-1=37.4 -> -3.8 abs. latency improved ~18ms avg though.

kevin: interesting. did you also enable the new KV batching handshake? that changed a few things in the kernel path.

maria: yes we flipped kernel+tiling-handshake + evict-policy=aggressive for the canary.

ej: (typo) meant aj — but: can you paste the exact canary id and the startup flags?

maria: canary id: canary-2026-03-14-orion7b-fp8-l40s. launch flags: `--fp8-enable=1 --tiling=handshake-v2 --kv-persist=0 --batcher=continuous-small`

evan: quick thought — AWQ/GPTQ fallback paths can produce different residual scaling. if quantizer calibration was done on shorter contexts we might see prefix bleed when handshake tiling interacts with KV cache eviction.

aj: try rerunning with `--kv-persist=1` (disable eviction between requests) for a quick check. if accuracy recovers it's likely an eviction/placement artifact rather than numeric precision per se.

maria: ran that: with kv_persist=1 rouge-1=40.9 (approx back to baseline), latency +6ms. so looks tied to eviction interplay.

kevin: that matches a suspicion: when eviction happens mid-response, the kernel may switch a codepath that uses a different accumulation order (float32 accumulate vs fp8 fused) for the final blocks. small numerical reorderings can cascade in autoregressive decoding.

jun: can you capture a short diff of logits for a failing sample (prefix+seed) between persisted and eviction runs? even a single prompt would help.

maria: pasted one sample diff below:```
# sample id: s-9832
step 45 - top token logit (persist): -2.12
step 45 - top token logit (evict):    -2.87
delta: -0.75 (softmax prob diff ~0.12)
```

aj: wow that's sizable. also check the kernel trace for which GEMM path was used pre/post-evict. ops-bot should have the trace tag in the canary logs.

ops-bot: deploy canary-2026-03-14-orion7b-fp8-l40s status: 5 nodes active, 0 errors, traces: https://ci.redwood.example/canary-2026-03-14-orion7b-fp8-l40s/traces

kevin: if we confirm it's a codepath flip we have two mitigation routes: 1) make eviction safe by forcing consistent accumulation path (costly), or 2) restrict eviction policy in FP8 mode and accept a small latency bump.

evan: another angle: re-run with `--quant-calib-mode=online` (recalibrate scale factors using short warmup) — if that recovers most of the delta it's a quantizer mismatch exacerbated by eviction timing.

maria: queued `online` run now. will also push a tiny canary with kv_persist=1 to dedicated pool.

jun: let's also add a tiny eval harness that reproduces multi-request eviction (shadow traffic) — that's the pattern we missed last rollout.

kevin: agreed. add an invariant check in the runtime that logs if accumulation order changes mid-request (low overhead flag). we can enable for canaries only.

maria: noted. next steps: 1) confirm kernel-path flip via traces, 2) run online-calib job, 3) kv_persist canary, 4) add runtime invariant. will post results later today. :white_check_mark:
